transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-29 09:30 PST
Duration: 1h15m (approx)
Location: Zoom / internal enablement room
Attendees: Lena Park (AE), Samir Patel (SE), Viv Chen (SE), Jordan Miller (Field Leader), Priya Kapoor (Senior AE), Ethan Lowe (PMM)

Summary:
Quick, scenario-driven enablement focused on competitive positioning vs Anthropic/OpenAI, demo triage for VPC/private deployments, and rapid roleplay of tricky pricing/latency objections. Goal: produce updated battlecard, micro-demo, and two customer scenarios for Jan rehearsals.

Topics covered:
- Competitive thesis and positioning hooks
- Demo checklist for private deployment (VPC, KMS, audit logs)
- Rapid-fire roleplay: price vs latency objections
- Hand-off artifacts and next steps

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Lena: Okay folks, thanks for coming in early, uh, we're running 75 minutes today, lot to get through so we'll keep it tight. Samir, Viv, you good for a quick mic check?
[00:00:18] Samir: Yep, all good. Can everyone see my screen? I'm gonna pull up the draft battlecard.
[00:00:24] Priya: Yup, good here. Slight echo but fine.
[00:00:30] Viv: Echo gone, good.
[00:00:34] Jordan: Hey, quick note, we're focused on two large finserv prospects this quarter so anything that touches audit logs, K M S, and V P C is gold.
[00:00:48] Lena: Great callout. Alright Samir, walk us through the competitive map, highlight where we pivot to dedicated or private.
[00:00:55] Samir: Cool. So slide one is the quick framing: on one axis is latency and predictability, other axis is unit cost. Anthropic and OpenAI tend to be strong on model quality but price and variable latency on large seq lengths can be an issue. Our angle is production economics — we lean on Dedicated and Private for predictability + observability, plus smart batching and KV cash, sorry KV cache, to cut token spend.
[00:01:25] Ethan: Did you say KV cash? (laughs)
[00:01:28] Samir: Yeah, sorry, bad transcript joke, KV cache, it's the thing that saves us on repeat context.
[00:01:33] Priya: Customers will ask directly, like 'why would we pick Redwood over Anthropic for compliance-heavy workloads' — do we have a pithy line?
[00:01:44] Viv: Short answer: same-ish model quality but we give deterministic SLOs and controls for cost. Longer: we do private deployments with customer-managed KMS, audit logs, and region pinning—so it's about serving guarantees not just model access.
[00:02:02] Jordan: And on the cost side, do we quantify typical savings or is it more qualitative?
[00:02:07] Samir: We do both. For workloads with high request-parallelism and repeat prefixes, our batching + prefix caching can cut per-token cost 20-40% over naive hosted endpoints. We'll follow up with a spreadsheet example. (note: spreadsheet link to be attached)
[00:02:25] Lena: Good. Okay let's move to demo triage — what are the must-show items when customers ask about Private/VPC? Viv, take this.
[00:02:33] Viv: I usually go through: 1) network isolation (V P C peering, private link), 2) key management (bring-your-own K M S / H S M), 3) auditability (immutable audit logs), 4) upgrade and rollback policies (canary and automatic fallback), 5) SLAs and support model. For demos we need a short script that shows login, a quick inference against a policy model, then show logs and KMS handshake.
[00:03:05] Priya: For demos where the customer is security-first, they often want to know about on-prem vs VPC. Do we have a clean flow to recommend one vs the other?
[00:03:14] Samir: Yes — VPC is usually faster to onboard and keeps control plane isolated but still uses our managed runtime. On-prem is for extremely regulated or air-gapped needs — longer lead time, different contract. We'll include a decision tree in the playbook.
[00:03:31] Jordan: Can we show a quick benchmark comparison in the demo? Like 99th percentile latency heatmap?
[00:03:36] Samir: We can, but heavy data. Better to show a simplified table in demo, like median vs 95th or 99th for modeled traffic. If they ask for full numbers, we hand off to SRE for a benchmark run.
[00:03:52] Lena: Okay switching gears to roleplay. Priya will take buyer persona #1 — cost-sensitive mid-market — and Jordan will be finserv security lead. We'll do two quick 5-min rounds. First round starts now.
[00:04:05] Priya: (as buyer) Hey, we looked at Redwood and Anthropic, Anthropic seems cheaper on their list price, why pay more?
[00:04:13] Viv: (as rep) Totally fair. If you look at total cost of ownership, you need to account for the variance in latency and retries, plus the engineering time to implement and maintain prefix caching yourself. Redwood delivers batching, KV cache out of the box and a model routing policy so your costs are more predictable.
[00:04:33] Priya: They push back — 'we can just use hosted and spin up reserved capacity if needed'
[00:04:39] Samir: Sure, reserved capacity helps but if you need private deployments for compliance or on-prem, that's a different plane. Also, we can do mixed routing: keep a cheap hosted model for general use and fall back to dedicated/private for sensitive requests — that hybrid routing reduces spend while ensuring compliance.
[00:04:57] Priya: Noted. The price objection didn't land badly.
[00:05:02] Lena: Round two — Jordan as finserv sec lead, send it.
[00:05:06] Jordan: (as buyer) Our compliance team will require SOC2 Type II, ISO, immutable logs, KMS integration. How do you prove that?
[00:05:18] Viv: We have SOC2 in the hosted control plane; for Private we provide the private control plane package with audit logs and KMS integration and we'll sign into contract language for retention and access. We can show a runbook demo: login, show an audit event, show the KMS key rotation entry.
[00:05:36] Jordan: Any gotchas?
[00:05:38] Samir: Occasionally customers misconfigure routing and think traffic leaves their VPC — we emphasize diagramming the network flows. Also data residency: if you need EU-only, we pin region and show proofs.
[00:05:53] Lena: Great. Let's capture typical shaky moments — what are the common stumps: 1) customers ask for 100% identical model behavior across private and hosted, 2) confusion about our quantization/accuracy tradeoffs, 3) price vs latency math.
[00:06:08] Viv: On the identical-model expectation — explain that we operate validated model variants. When customers need bit-for-bit parity we recommend an in-place validation run and possibly a pinned variant. Don't overpromise.
[00:06:21] Priya: About quantization, they ask if quantized models change hallucination rates — what's the right short answer?
[00:06:28] Samir: Short answer: sometimes, but our Optimize tool recommends the right quantization profile by workload and we keep an eval suite to catch regressions. Use evals tied to their prompt sets.
[00:06:40] Ethan: Can we show a one-slide flow: when to recommend Hosted, Dedicated, Private?
[00:06:45] Lena: Yes — new slide added to the battlecard. Samir, you own that slide.
[00:06:49] Samir: Got it.
[00:06:51] Lena: Okay we're down to the rapid-fire rebuttal table — we'll run through three objections and assign rebuttals.
[00:06:57] Viv: Objection A: 'We need 24/7 support for latency incidents at 99th pctl' — rebuttal: dedicated SLA with support add-on and route-based fallbacks, plus tracing hooks and token-level costs so we can debug patterns.
[00:07:14] Priya: Objection B: 'Our legal team won't sign because of data retention policy' — rebuttal: we offer customizable retention windows and can document retention in contract, show audit log examples.
[00:07:28] Jordan: Objection C: 'We're worried about vendor lock with proprietary runtime' — rebuttal: our serving runtime is hardware-optimized but supports open model formats and we provide export/hand-off docs; plus the economic benefit buys time.
[00:07:44] Samir: Quick note — sometimes the 'export' sentence gets misheard; emphasize we support standard formats (ONNX, GGUF where applicable).
[00:07:55] Lena: Alright artifact checklist: battlecard (owner Lena), micro-demo (owner Samir), roleplay scenarios (owner Jordan). Attach links in the follow-up email.
[00:08:08] Ethan: For the micro-demo, can we include a short network diagram and the KMS handshake? That would be the most convincing for finserv.
[00:08:15] Samir: Yes. I'll script it: show VPC peering, initiate a signed request to our runtime, show a KMS decrypt event in the audit panel.
[00:08:27] Priya: Timeboxing note — the micro-demo should be 7 minutes max.
[00:08:30] Viv: Also include alternate paths if customers ask for on-prem: high-level time-to-value and contract differences.
[00:08:40] Jordan: One more, do we want to bake in a short bench of competitor rebuttals? Like a two-line mention for Anthropic vs OpenAI?
[00:08:48] Lena: Yes, add a competitor-tactics table to the battlecard. Viv, a few lines each.
[00:08:55] Viv: Will do.
[00:09:00] [Silence / notes taking for ~2 minutes]
[00:11:10] Lena: Quick logistics: we'll send the follow-up with links, action items, and schedule the external rehearsal. Any other sticky points?
[00:11:20] Priya: Can we get a one-pager that lists 'what to demo' for each buyer persona?
[00:11:25] Samir: Yes, we'll make one for finserv, healthcare, and mid-market.
[00:11:30] Jordan: Also add a callout for 'when to escalate to SRE for benchmarks' — that's important.
[00:11:35] Lena: Noted. Alright if no more, thanks everyone, we'll reconvene virtually on Jan 9 for the customer rehearsal.
[00:11:44] All: Thanks!
